current_status.stage: Approved; market leader across monthly (Sustenna), 3-month (Trinza) and 6-month (Hafyera) paliperidone palmitate formulations
current_status.dosing_target: Monthly / Every 3 months / Every 6 months (paliperidone palmitate)
current_status.data_point: Q2 2026 Invega franchise (Sustenna/Xeplion/Trinza/Trevicta) net sales $1.02B, +2.3% YoY, per J&J Q2 2026 earnings

finding_history.summary: FDA approved Invega Hafyera (6-month paliperidone palmitate), the first and only twice-yearly LAI for schizophrenia, rounding out the Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera dosing-interval ladder.

FDA approved Erzofri (Luye Pharma), a competing branded paliperidone palmitate extended-release injectable suspension for schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder — the first patented paliperidone palmitate LAI developed in China to reach the US market, directly competing with the Invega franchise.

Luye Pharma launched Erzofri commercially in the US, marketed with a single-dose (351 mg) initiation advantage over standard monthly paliperidone palmitate products that require two initiation doses — a direct competitive positioning against Invega Sustenna.

Janssen v. Sun Pharma Hatch-Waxman patent litigation (D.N.J., re: US9439906B2 covering paliperidone palmitate ER injectable formulations) closed via consent judgment: Sun admitted the patent valid/enforceable/infringed and accepted a permanent injunction against launching its ANDA product before patent expiry — a near-term generic threat deferred, exact authorized-entry date confidential. A parallel Delaware case against Sun was separately dismissed without prejudice in Oct 2025.
J&J Q2 2026 earnings: Invega franchise (Sustenna/Xeplion/Trinza/Trevicta) net sales rose 2.3% year-over-year to $1.02 billion, within J&J's broader raised full-year 2026 outlook.
